The Aurora Borealis Problem Solved. On Sunday night and Monday morning there was an unusually brilliant exhibition OF the Aurora Borealia, which covered one half the Northern heavens, from East 20 West. This mysterious light has ever puz- z led natural philosophers, who have ad- vanced the most contradictory explanations Tor the phenomena. Some have ascribed ihem To the reiraction of the SUMS rays from Arctic ice bergs; others have believed that the refraclion is from Northern ice or snow, and the Iremulous motion to be caus- I'd by the perpetual vibrations of the earth's atnoSOhere; but The magnetic telegraph mas solved the prob i'm. On Sunday even ing, when the sky was perfectly clear, the stars shining and the wind still, the only unusual appearance being the reddening of lie Northern and Eastern heavens. one of the operators N the Harrsburyn Office chaaced to lodch the wire. and was thrown, by the viole nee of shock which he re- ceived, across the room. 1T :he; same time the Superintendent Of the Cansdiap lines Of telegraph informs US that the line betwe en- Quebec and Farther Point was in perle ct working order. Yet it was proved impos: Nsible to despatch the foreign news across the wires. The Aurora Borealis had so charged the air with electricity as to par italy destroy the insulation The pheno- mena of the Northern Lights, may, there fore. be ascribed to electricity, and long disputed question of science is definitely y explained d.-PiHSburqh Post.

N. de Ia Rive, the celebrated French astron. mer, explains the production of the aurora bore alis in the following manner When the sun, having passed INTO the south. ern hemisphere, the 5queous vapors which have accumulated during the summer in this part of the atmosphere begin TO condense, the kind of humid cap enyeloping the polar regions ex- tends more and more, and facilitates the passage Of the electricity accumulated in the upper portions of the air But in those elevated re- gions, and especially at this season of the year, tue aqueous vapors must frequently pass into the state of minute particles of ice or snow floating in the air, similar 10 those which give rise to the halos they form, as it were, a kind of semi transparent mist. These half frozen fogs conduct The electricity to the surface of the earth, near the pole, and are at the same time illuminated by these currents or electric discharges. In fact all observers agree in asser- ting that aurora borealis is constantly preceded by mist, which rises from the pole and the margins of which, less dense than the remain der are colored the first and indeed it is very near the pole in the wint MONTHS and espes cially in those where there is an abundance of vapor in the air. Mr.. Merriam, the Brooklyn meteor-wise, has pronounced his opinion of the Boreal lights He says ''the Aurora( electricity discharged from the craters of volcanos) either dissolves in the atmosphere, and is thus diffused through space, or concentrated into gelatinous substance form. ing Reteors, called shooting stars. These me teors dissolve rapidly in atmospheric air, but sometimes reach the earth before dissolying, and resemble thin starch" Merriam is easi. ly humbugged if not humbug, for he claims to have a bit of the Aurora in his possession, which so resembles silk that he styles it the silkery of the skies" The auroral display at Boston after midnight on the ID, was so brilliant that ordinary print could be,,read, and considerably impeded the wor- !; =, Of the telegraph up to noon of the 2d. At times the current from east to west was so reg ular that messages could be sent over the lines without the usual batteries being applied The operators in Pittsburgh and Philadelphia transmitted auroral messages to each other, and at intervals kept up lively chat by the same medium, the galyanic batteries being cut off and the instruments worked exclusively by means of the auroral electricity. 1t was exact ly similar in its effects, though differing in kind, to that generated in telegraphic batteries or what is known as common atmospheric elec tricity. The Pittsburgh Chronicle says; This, it is believed, is the first and only in stance on record, where the Aurora itself--beau- tiful, glorious and mysterious as it has always been considered in its brilliant manifestations has actually been harnessed up and been com pelleI to do the errands of man.
